questions.question_text: A digital badge selector has outcome probabilities $\frac{1}{8},\frac{3}{8},\frac{4}{8}$. What is their total?

options.why: Leaves out the first probability and adds only three eighths and four eighths.
Adds both numerators and denominators, giving eight twenty-fourths before simplifying.
Keeps the common denominator but ignores the sum of the three numerators.

questions.question_text: A route app selects hill, coast or valley. $P(\text{hill})=\frac{2}{9}$ and $P(\text{coast})=\frac{4}{9}$. Find $P(\text{valley})$ as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Subtracts only the coast probability from one and ignores the hill outcome.
Adds the two known probabilities and reports their total instead of the remainder.
Copies the hill probability and assumes the missing outcome must match it.

questions.question_text: A learning app gives a bonus question with probability $\frac{4}{11}$. Find the probability that it does not give a bonus question, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Repeats the probability of a bonus instead of finding the opposite outcome.
Subtracts one too many when taking four favourable parts away from eleven.
Finds seven remaining parts but places the original four in the denominator.

questions.question_text: A screen animation has three listed outcome probabilities: $\frac{4}{10},\frac{5}{10},\frac{3}{10}$. Which diagnosis is correct?

options.text: The list is impossible because its total is $\frac{6}{5}$, above $1$.
The list is valid because every individual fraction is below $1$.
options.why: Checks each value separately but fails to check that all outcome probabilities total one.

options.text: The list is incomplete because its total is below $1$.
options.why: Assumes a missing outcome without adding the numerators to get twelve tenths.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{4}{10}+\frac{5}{10}+\frac{3}{10}$
$=\frac{12}{10}$
$=\frac{6}{5}>1$
The list cannot contain all outcome probabilities.

questions.question_text: A sound selector lists probabilities $\frac{1}{8},\frac{2}{8},\frac{3}{8}$. By how much is the list short of $1$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Reports the total of the listed probabilities instead of the amount still missing.
Assumes one missing outcome must copy the smallest listed probability.
Subtracts only the largest listed probability from one and ignores the other two.

questions.question_text: A tool app opens a map with probability $\frac{1}{12}$ and a camera with probability $\frac{4}{12}$. Find the probability that it opens neither, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Adds map and camera probabilities but reports that combined event instead of its complement.
Subtracts only the camera probability from one and ignores the map probability.
Subtracts only the map probability from one and ignores the camera probability.

questions.question_text: A digital chooser has four outcomes. Two have probabilities $\frac{2}{10}$ and $\frac{4}{10}$. The other two outcomes are equally likely. Find the probability of each remaining outcome, as a fraction in simplest form.

options.why: Finds the whole remaining probability but assigns all of it to each missing outcome.
Averages the two known probabilities instead of sharing the remaining probability.
Shares the four remaining tenths among all four outcomes instead of the two missing ones.

questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{two remaining})=1-\frac{2}{10}-\frac{4}{10}$
$=\frac{4}{10}$
Each remaining outcome has probability $\frac{2}{10}=\frac{1}{5}$.
